Geometric Interpretation of the Linear Span
?

The linear span of vectors can be interpreted geometrically as the points in space that can be reached by adding multiples of those vectors.

  • The span of a single nonzero vector is a line through the origin. More precisely, if then determines the line with direction vector that passes through the origin. For instance, if then represents the line spanned by
  • The span of two non-parallel vectors is a plane through the origin. More precisely, if ( and are not parallel), then determines the plane with direction vectors and that passes through the origin. For instance, if then represents the plane spanned by and
